intro: New to Columbia? This walkthrough orders the official steps for a Social Security number and Missouri ID — so you know what to do before you visit an office.
disclaimer: Rules differ for international vs. domestic students. Always confirm with ISSS or the office listed on each step before you go.

phases.label: Before you start
phases.summary: Gather immigration documents and check whether you need ISSS signatures first.

steps.title: Read the official ISSS identification guide
steps.detail: Mizzou's International Student & Scholar Services explains SSN and Missouri license requirements, office addresses, and which forms you need.

steps.title: Collect your core documents
steps.detail: Keep your passport, visa, I-94, and I-20 or DS-2019 accessible. You will need them for both SSN and license appointments.

steps.title: Contact ISSS if you're unsure
steps.detail: If you are not employed, on OPT, or unsure which ID you need, ask an international adviser before visiting SSA or the license office.

phases.label: Social Security Number (SSN)
phases.summary: Required for most employed students. International students must have a job offer and wait two weeks after U.S. entry.

steps.title: Confirm you have a job offer
steps.detail: International students can only apply for an SSN if they are authorized to work (on-campus job, CPT, etc.). No job offer means no SSN application yet.

steps.title: Wait two full weeks after entering the U.S.
steps.detail: SSA will not process your application until at least 14 days after your most recent U.S. entry date on your I-94.

steps.title: Get an employment verification letter
steps.detail: Request the letter through myStatus. Your employer signs it, then bring it to ISSS for their signature before visiting SSA.

steps.title: Visit the Columbia Social Security office
steps.detail: Bring your signed employment letter, passport, I-94, and I-20/DS-2019 to 3402 Buttonwood Drive, Columbia.

phases.label: Missouri driver's license or nondriver ID
phases.summary: Need to drive or want a state photo ID? Missouri requires tests plus documents from ISSS and possibly SSA.

steps.title: Request a letter of good standing (international students)
steps.detail: Use myStatus to request the letter ISSS provides for the license office. Domestic students can skip this ISSS step.

steps.title: Get a letter of ineligibility if you have no SSN
steps.detail: Missouri requires either your SSN or an SSA letter stating you are not eligible for one yet. Visit the Buttonwood Dr SSA office if needed.

steps.title: Pass vision, road sign, and written tests
steps.detail: Schedule and complete testing with the Missouri State Highway Patrol before applying at the license office.

steps.title: Apply at the Columbia License Office
steps.detail: Bring all immigration documents, your test results, and SSN or ineligibility letter to 403 Vandiver Drive. Nondriver ID uses the same office if you will not drive.

phases.label: Getting around without a car
phases.summary: While you settle in, use Mizzou's shuttle and Columbia's public buses to reach campus and downtown.

steps.title: Track Tiger Line and Go COMO buses live
steps.detail: Download the ETA Transit app or use Go COMO's website for real-time bus locations. Tiger Line loops campus seven days a week during the semester.
